summary: Santa Barbara County lookout staffed by the Forest Service from 1935 to 1939 per newspaper quotes; FFLA lists it as gone. No account of the site today found.

facts.design: Lookout tower reached by 13 steps (1938 newspaper)
facts.agency: Los Padres National Forest (called the Santa Barbara National Forest in 1936)
facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no source read gives a date or cause

events.note: Earliest staffing in the sources read: a man from Paso Robles sent to the lookout in June 1935
Conrad Munson sent a daily report from the lookout
Warren Rice was the Forest Service lookout
Lightning struck between the station and a nearby flagpole in October 1937; officials feared fires that night, but the report describes no fire
Bert Feehan began lookout duties on June 16, 1938, the day the new radio and telephone links were set up
Feehan finished his lookout work in November 1939; the last staffing in the sources read

notes_for_editor: Built date, design beyond the 13 steps, and the date and cause of the loss are all unknown. History rests on newspaper quotes reproduced on the Forest Lookouts page; the original newspapers were not read. Do not confuse with the Manzanita Mountain lookout in Modoc County (FFLA NHLR US 1332, CA 155), which is a different, standing site. The 1936 and 1937 pages quote staff by name; those names are historical and from the newspapers only.
